title: Preparation and Characterization of Lipophilic Doxorubicin Pro-drug Micelles
protocol: Weigh 390 mg of doxorubicin and 243 mg of palmitic acid hydrazide.
Transfer the weighed materials to a round bottom flask.
Add 150 ml of anhydrous methanol to the flask using a glass syringe.
Pipette 39 µl of trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) into the flask.
Stir the reaction mixture for 18 hours at room temperature in the dark using a magnetic stirrer.
Remove the solvent from the reaction mixture with a rotary evaporator.
Add 3 g of silica gel when the volume of the mixture is reduced to around 20 ml.
Continue rotary evaporation until dry powders form, allowing adsorption onto silica gel.
Keep the sample under vacuum for an additional 30 minutes after forming dry powders.
Pack 50 g of silica gel into a column using dichloromethane as solvent.
Carefully add the silica gel sample containing adsorbed product to the column.
Elute the column with a mixture of dichloromethane and methanol, gradually increasing methanol percentage.
Collect fractions of eluent in test tubes (25 ml/tube).
Monitor the progress by thin layer chromatography (TLC).
Combine all fractions containing pure DOX-PA and remove the solvent using a rotary evaporator until dry powder is formed.
Further dry the product under vacuum overnight.
Cut a 4 cm x 8 cm section of TLC plate.
Spot sample solutions 0.5 cm from the bottom of the plate with TLC spotting capillaries using methanol as the solvent.
Place the TLC plate into a developing chamber containing a mixture of dichloromethane and methanol (3/1, v/v).
Remove the plate when the solvent front reaches the top of the plate.
Mark the location of the solvent front with a pencil.
Allow the plate to dry completely.
Place the TLC plate into a staining chamber containing saturated iodine vapor to visualize samples.
Dissolve DSPE-PEG (40 mg) and DOX-PA (4 mg) in 2 ml of methanol in a 10 ml glass vial.
Remove the organic solvent under vacuum using a rotary evaporator until a thin film forms in the vial.
Evaporate organic solvents under inert gas to form a film.
Transfer 2 ml of Dulbecco's phosphate buffered saline (pH 7.4, DPBS) to the glass vial.
Place the vial in an ultrasonic bath for 3 min at room temperature.
Keep micelles at 4 °C for short-term storage and -20 °C for long-term storage.
Dissolve DOX-PA synthesized previously in DMSO to prepare solutions of 1 µg/ml, 5 µg/ml, 20 µg/ml, 50 µg/ml, and 100 µg/ml.
Measure the absorption of each DOX-PA solution with a UV-VIS spectrometer at 490 nm.
Generate a standard curve based on the DOX-PA drug concentrations and their corresponding absorption at 490 nm.
Dilute 25 μl of drug-loaded micelle with 500 μl of DMSO.
Measure absorption at 490 nm with a UV-VIS spectrometer.
Calculate drug concentrations using the standard curve generated in section 3.1.1.
Calculate encapsulation efficiency using the equation: Drug Encapsulation Efficiency (%) = (amount of drugs in micelles) / (amount of added drug) × 100%.
Dilute micelles with DPBS (pH 7.4) to a final DSPE-PEG concentration of 1 mg/ml.
Analyze a 2 ml sample with a particle size analyzer to obtain the Z-average size and polydispersity index (PDI).
Remove cell culture medium from a cell culture flask containing DU-145 human prostate cancer cells.
Rinse cells with 2 ml of DPBS (pH 7.4).
Aspirate DPBS, add 1 ml of trypsin solution (0.25%), and incubate for 2 min at 37 °C to detach the cells.
Add 10 ml of cell culture medium when most cells are detached from the flask.
Transfer cells to a 15-ml centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the cells at 1,000 x g for 5 min.
Re-suspend the cell pellet with 5 ml of cell culture medium.
Remove a sample for counting cell numbers with a hemocytometer.
Dilute the cells with cell culture medium to a density of 50,000 cells/ml.
Add diluted-cell suspensions into a 96-well cell culture plate (100 µl/well).
Incubate the cells in a cell culture incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 18 hours to allow cell attachment.
Dilute DOX DMSO solution with cell culture medium to obtain final drug concentrations of 0.1 µM, 0.5 µM, 2 µM, 5 µM, and 10 µM.
Keep the final DMSO concentration in all samples at 0.5%.
Dilute DOX-PA micelle with cell culture medium to obtain final drug concentrations of 0.1 µM, 0.5 µM, 2 µM, 5 µM, and 10 µM.
Use the blank cell culture medium as a control.
Remove the 96-well cell culture plate from the incubator after 18 hours.
Replace the cell culture medium with 100 µl of medium containing different treatment agents.
Incubate the cells in the cell culture incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for an additional 72 hours.
Aspirate the medium from the wells.
Add 100 µl of medium containing 0.5 mg/ml of 3-(4,5-dimethyl-thiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyl tetrazolium bromide (MTT).
Incubate the cells in the cell culture incubator for an additional 2 hours.
Carefully remove the medium from the cells.
Add 100 µl of DMSO to dissolve formazan crystals.
Measure absorbance with the microplate spectrophotometer at a wavelength of 570 nm and a reference wavelength of 670 nm.
Calculate the cell viability using the equation: Cell Viability (%) = (ATest ⁄ Acontrol) × 100%.
